request: Our school library wants a simple catalogue of its books. The librarian should be able to add a book with its title, its author and how many copies the library owns. Students should be able to see all the books, and look at one book to see how many copies are still on the shelf. A student borrows a book by giving their name, and returns it when they are done; a student can only return a book they actually borrowed. When every copy of a book is out, nobody else can borrow it until a copy comes back.
summary:
I've built the library catalogue in `app.py`. All 18 automated tests pass. They cover every endpoint and every rule in the plan you approved. The books and loans are saved in a file called `library.db` in the same folder, which is created when the app starts.

**What you can do with it:**
- **`POST /books`** – the librarian adds a book by sending `{"title", "author", "copies"}`. The reply shows the book with its book number, the copies owned and how many are on the shelf.
- **`GET /books`** – lists all books, each with how many copies are on the shelf.
- **`GET /books/{bookNumber}`** – shows one book: title, author, copies owned and copies on the shelf.
- **`POST /books/{bookNumber}/borrow`** – a student sends `{"name": "..."}` to borrow one copy. The reply shows the loan number and the updated book.
- **`POST /books/{bookNumber}/return`** – a student sends `{"name": "..."}` to return a copy they borrowed. The reply shows the updated book.

**What gets refused:**
- **A new book with something missing or invalid:** a missing or blank title or author, or a number of copies that isn't a whole number of at least 1.
- **A book that isn't in the catalogue:** looking at it, borrowing it or returning it.
- **Borrowing or returning without a name.**
- **Borrowing when every copy is out.** It works again once a copy comes back.
- **Returning a book the student doesn't currently have.** This includes returning the same copy twice.

**Things you should know:**
- **Who can use it:** as in the plan, nothing checks who is using the system. Anyone could add a book or borrow under another student's name.
- **Matching names:** a return only works if the name matches the one used to borrow exactly, including capitals and small letters ("Ann" and "ann" count as different students). Two students with the same name would also count as one person.
- **Borrowing more than one copy:** a student can borrow several copies of the same book. Your request didn't say this should be stopped.
- **Privacy:** students' names are stored but never shown in the book lists or details. That keeps who has which book private until you answer the question about it in the plan.

The other open questions from the plan, about checking that only the librarian adds books and about changing or removing books, are still waiting for your answer. None of them is built yet.

plan.summary: This plan sets up a simple online catalogue for your school library. The librarian can add books (title, author and number of copies owned). Students can see every book, open one book to see how many copies are still on the shelf, borrow a copy by giving their name, and return it later. The system tracks who has which book so that only a student who actually borrowed a book can return it, and nobody can borrow a book when every copy is out. Nothing in your request was unsafe or unrelated, so nothing was left out. Questions for you, not included in this plan: (1) As asked, nothing checks who is using the system, so anyone could add a book or borrow under another student's name. Would you like a way to make sure only the librarian can add books? (2) Students' names are stored with what they borrowed. Should other students be able to see who has a book, or should that stay private? (3) Two students could share the same name. Is a name alone enough, or should students also give something like their class? (4) Should the librarian be able to change or remove a book later, for example if a copy is lost?

data.name: Book
fields: Book number (given automatically, used to find the book)
Number of copies the library owns
Copies still on the shelf (worked out automatically: copies owned minus copies currently borrowed)

data.name: Loan (a record that a student has a copy of a book)
fields: Name of the student who borrowed it
Whether it has been returned yet

endpoints.does: The librarian adds a new book by giving its title, its author and how many copies the library owns.
Shows the list of all books in the catalogue.
Shows one book: its title, author, how many copies the library owns and how many are still on the shelf.
A student borrows one copy of this book by giving their name. One fewer copy is then on the shelf.
A student returns a copy of this book they borrowed by giving their name. One more copy is then back on the shelf.

rules: A new book is refused if its title, author or number of copies is missing.
A new book is refused if the number of copies is not a whole number of at least one.
Looking at, borrowing or returning a book that is not in the catalogue is refused.
Borrowing is refused if the student does not give their name.
Borrowing is refused when every copy of the book is already out; it becomes possible again once a copy is returned.
Returning is refused if the student does not give their name.
Returning is refused if that student does not currently have a copy of that book borrowed.
